findings.cause: Source: security S1 (P2, non-blocking). SYMPTOM: the unapproved what-if exercises prod ARM access. CAUSE: the WhatIf job's AzureCLI@2 at stage-template.yml:34 uses parameters.azureServiceConnection. That is the same connection that runs az deployment sub create (:72) and az webapp deploy (:137), and azure-pipelines.yml:77 binds it to sc-policies-prod, a connection with subscription-scope write rights. The what-if needs read plus the deployment what-if action only. INTERACTION WITH I1: the I1 restructure makes the unapproved what-if a deliberate design property, not an accident of job order, so this question has to be settled as part of it. S1's alternative, an approval check on the service connection, conflicts with I1. Checks are evaluated for every protected resource a stage uses, so an approval on the shared ARM connection would gate the what-if stage too and reproduce the QA defect. Non-approval checks that evaluate automatically, such as branch control, don't conflict. ANSWER: yes, the restructured what-if stage should get its own lower-privilege ARM connection per environment, passed as a separate template parameter. It is the only S1 remedy that keeps the approval after the what-if. Two caveats. (1) I understand Reader alone isn't enough for what-if, because it needs Microsoft.Resources/deployments/whatIf/action at subscription scope, and possibly the validate action, beyond */read. A custom role (Reader plus those actions) is likely needed. Verify this against the ARM what-if permissions doc before writing it down. (2) This adds three out-of-repo prerequisites: a connection and role assignment per environment. Those belong with the other prerequisites in QA section C, and in the README carry-over to F6. It's David's call, because S1 is P2: he may instead record the shared connection as an accepted residual risk next to the existing one (stage-template.yml:93-95), naming the merge-to-main exposure. Either way, record that the policies-<env> variable group, also used before approval (:27), must stay secret-free and carry no approval check. FIX DIRECTION: decide (separate what-if connection, or recorded acceptance). If separate, the what-if stage's azureSubscription is a distinct template parameter, never the deploy one, and the pipeline passes one per environment.

findings.cause: Reviewer R1 (P1). The schema has no docs layer, so I used 'api' because the sentence describes API behaviour. Symptom: docs/design.md:64-65 says that ?REFERENCE=x comes back keyed 'reference' and that 'That is the JSON naming policy applied to the key.' Cause: a guess from a QA note was carried forward as fact, and nobody in the chain checked it against the code. WHAT THE REPO PROVES about ?REFERENCE: (a) RejectUnknownQueryParametersFilter.cs:13-17 treats as known only parameters whose binding source is Query, compared case-insensitively. On GET /policies/{reference} the reference is bound from the route, so any query key named reference, in any case, is unknown and gives a 400. A test pins this only for lower case: RetrieveNotFoundTests.cs:84-95 sends ?reference=X and asserts the errors key 'reference'. No test sends REFERENCE. (b) The filter adds the error under the key exactly as the client sent it (RejectUnknownQueryParametersFilter.cs:25). (c) The only key rewrite in the repo is ValidationProblems.cs:15 with :25-26, which lower-cases the first character of each dotted segment and nothing else. On that code alone, 'REFERENCE' would become 'rEFERENCE'. (d) Program.cs:50-56 sets no PropertyNamingPolicy and no DictionaryKeyPolicy, and the comment at PoliciesController.cs:93 records that ValidationProblem() does not camel-case keys. (e) The only evidence for the key 'reference' is one observation by hand, docs/qa/build-F2.md:214-217, which says 'That looks like…' and 'no test covers it'. Taken together, the repo proves the 400 by design, but not by a test for upper case. It proves the 'reference' key only as one unpinned observation, and it proves no cause at all. The repo's own key rewrite cannot produce 'reference', so the key comes from framework model-state key handling that the repo neither documents nor tests. WHERE IT CAME FROM: all three places. (1) The docs' sources: the guess at build-F2.md:216 was hardened into a stated cause in the F2 sign-off row (docs/qa/build-F2.md:239, '(camelCase naming policy)'), then in the F2 context save (docs/context/20261019-001302-f2-done-merged.md:44) and the F3 carry-over. (2) The brief: the t1 title (docs/plans/active/build.dag.yaml:356) tells the builder to state 'validation error keys are camelCase (an unknown query key ?REFERENCE is reported as reference)' and gives no instruction to verify it. (3) The builder's method: builder a69aae2b077cc01b3 searched tests for a pinning test (docs/trace/build/F6/activity.jsonl:33), found none, then grepped build-F2.md for 'camel' (activity.jsonl:34) and wrote the cause. It did this after reading the contradicting PoliciesController.cs:93 (activity.jsonl:32) and docs/qa/build-F4.md:270-273, 'Measured over HTTP, it didn't' (activity.jsonl:34). No builder ever opened ValidationProblems.cs or the filter: in activity.jsonl only the reviewer and the investigators read them. The rewriter of d72bf26 (a8b79244630f23b2d) read no code at all before writing docs/design.md (activity.jsonl:67-85). RECURRENCE: this is a new fingerprint, because no A1 finding cited it. The A1 route did not catch it for two reasons. Its scope was the link gate plus a pass on wording and numbers (findings/A1.md I2-I5). And the A1 builder edited only the five cited items, with no code reads (activity.jsonl:133-136). FIX DIRECTION: state only what the repo proves. An unknown query key is a 400 with an errors entry, and that includes a key that differs only in case from a route parameter. Drop the cause. If the ?REFERENCE example stays, either pin its key with a test first and state the pinned key, or say plainly that it was seen once by hand and is not pinned.

findings.cause: Security S2. The verdict cites docs/design.md:370; the actual lines are docs/design.md:195-196. Cause: configuration is stated as proven runtime behaviour. The repo proves only the trust configuration (Program.cs:21-31 and :83). Whether the App Service Linux front end connects from those ranges has never been tested, and infrastructure/README.md:141-142 says so. If it does not connect from them, X-Forwarded-For is ignored and every client shares one rate-limit partition (Program.cs:131-133). X-Forwarded-Proto is ignored too, so Request.IsHttps is false and the 400 at Program.cs:95-101 answers every request outside /health. The brief (build.dag.yaml:356) placed the 'httpsOnly and App Service forwarded headers' caveat under the F5 deployment notes only. Symptom: across rounds, the docs keep stating things the repo does not prove: A1 I2-I5, A2 R1-R4 and S2, and I2 and I7-I13 above. Each round's fix only touched the lines it was given. Cause: no step in the F6 loop traces each factual sentence in the docs to a file:line or a test. It includes the ?REFERENCE behaviour, the framing 'for David's review' and the internal ids. It gives no instruction to verify them and no instruction about the audience. (2) Builder a69aae2b077cc01b3 took its causes from QA notes and verdict notes (activity.jsonl:33-35). Builder a8b79244630f23b2d wrote README.md, docs/design.md and infrastructure/README.md with no code reads at all (activity.jsonl:67-85). Builder a523f301c8db0f1da, the A1 fix, read no code (activity.jsonl:133-136). (3) The orchestrator's gates check links, URLs, build, tests and scope only (loop.jsonl:6-13). (4) Each finding gets a fingerprint for one line, so the retry ladder never saw the same cause come back. On the hypothesis: it is confirmed for R1, R3 and I9 (secondary sources copied without checking) and for R4 (brief content), with two corrections. First, for R1 the docs' sources themselves already stated the guess as fact before F6 began: the signed F2 sign-off row (docs/qa/build-F2.md:239) and the context save (docs/context/20261019-001302-f2-done-merged.md:44). findings.cause: Reviewer R1, part 1 of 2. I split R1 in two on purpose; I2 covers the other half. There is no docs layer, so I use 'api' as in A2. SYMPTOM: docs/design.md:72-74 links the ?REFERENCE 400 to casing with 'so', then says 'By that code its key would be rEFERENCE'. The only observation, docs/qa/build-F2.md:214-217, saw 'reference'. CAUSE: the doc predicts the key from one file. The source of that reading is the A2 investigation itself. findings/A2.md:14, I1(c), says "On that code alone, 'REFERENCE' would become 'rEFERENCE'". I2 in the same file says "By the code, an unknown ?COLOUR=x would be keyed 'cOLOUR' (filter :25, then ValidationProblems.cs:26)". The builder copied that reasoning, and claims.json:518 cites 'ValidationProblems.cs:25-26 (code reading, not run)'. The reading skips a step the reviewer named. RejectUnknownQueryParametersFilter.cs:25 calls ModelState.AddModelError(key, ...), and ValidationProblems.cs:13 then builds the dictionary from ModelState. Nothing in the repo documents or tests how ModelState stores a key. A likely explanation, which is framework behaviour outside the repo and NOT for the docs: ModelState keys are case-insensitive, and the route binder has already recorded an entry 'reference'. So AddModelError('REFERENCE') would land on that entry and come back as 'reference', while ?COLOUR would still give 'cOLOUR'. If that is right, no single casing rule covers client keys, which is why the doc cannot generalise from code. The 'so' is false on the repo's own evidence. The 400 comes from the filter's binding-source test (RejectUnknownQueryParametersFilter.cs:12-17), not from casing, and lower-case ?reference=X gives the same 400 (RetrieveNotFoundTests.cs:84-95). RECURRENCE: same paragraph and same cause as A2 I1 (asserting the casing of the ?REFERENCE key, and a reason for it, without proof). Only the claimed reason changed, from a naming policy to a code reading, so I reuse I1's fingerprint. WHY THE INV-003 ROUTE DID NOT PREVENT IT: (1) The A2 findings put the code prediction and 'rEFERENCE' into the builder's inputs. (2) inv-003 rec 4 (inv-003.plan.md:40, accepted) says to pin the casing with tests 'before any doc states it'. No bug plan exists (docs/plans/active holds only build and inv-001..003), yet the doc states a casing. (3) The rewritten brief (build.dag.yaml:356) says to report error keys 'as the code does it'. That invites a code reading. (4) inv-003 rec 1 (inv-003.plan.md:37) allows 'marked observed/untested' as an alternative to removal. claims.json:8 used that to keep a prediction that contradicts the only observation. (5) claims.json:512 records the sentence as 'A client-sent key keeps the rest of its casing; unknown query key ... is a 400', with a semicolon where design.md:72 has 'so'. The table paraphrased away the causal word that the check most needed to catch. FIX DIRECTION: replace the whole bullet at docs/design.md:70-76 with wording that states only what is tested or plainly in the code, with no prediction and no 'so'. EXACT REPLACEMENT: '- **Validation error keys.** For a body or model error, the API lower-cases the first letter of each dot-separated segment of the key (`ValidationProblems.cs`); for example, the key for a policyholder’s date of birth is `policyholders[0].dateOfBirth`. A query key that the action does not bind from the query string is a `400`, with `Unknown query parameter.` under that key in `errors`. A key named after a route parameter is one of these: `GET /policies/{reference}?reference=X` is a `400` keyed `reference`. No test sends a query key in upper case, so the key returned for one is not specified. The renewal endpoint with no body writes its key, `amount`, by hand in the controller.' SOURCES, one per sentence: (a) ValidationProblems.cs:15 and :25-26, and tests/postman/Uinsure.Policies.postman_collection.json:2278 asserts errors has 'policyholders[0].dateOfBirth'. (b) RejectUnknownQueryParametersFilter.cs:12-17 and :23-25, and RetrieveNotFoundTests.cs:75-79 (colour, message). (c) RetrieveNotFoundTests.cs:90-94. (d) a grep of tests/ for an upper-case query key (pattern '\?[A-Z]{2,}[A-Za-z]*=' in *.cs and in the Postman collection) finds none. The 'so' in (d) rests on the absence of a test, which is provable, not on code behaviour. (e) PoliciesController.cs:91-95. Remove the '?REFERENCE', 'rEFERENCE' and 'keeps the rest of its casing' text, claims.json:512 and :518, and the rEFERENCE item in claims.json:8. If David wants the observation kept, the only allowed form is a standalone sentence: 'One manual check of `?REFERENCE=X` saw the key `reference` (`docs/qa/build-F2.md`).' Nothing may be joined to it by so, because or 'by the code'. A doc may state the casing of a client-sent key only after the rec-4 bug plan pins it.

(a) activity.jsonl:315 runs 'cat -n main.bicep modules/appservice.bicep modules/sql.bicep', and cat -n numbers straight through all three files. main.bicep is 102 lines, so appservice refs are +102 (httpsOnly is appservice.bicep:37, cited :139; Database__Provider is :46, cited :148). main plus appservice is 102+76=178, so sql refs are +178 (azureADOnlyAuthentication is sql.bicep:26, cited in the :198-205 block). (b) activity.jsonl:316 runs 'cat -n modules/network.bicep modules/monitoring.bicep'. network.bicep is 108 lines, so monitoring:134 is really :26, in a 27-line file. (c) activity.jsonl:329 runs 'cat -n azure-pipelines.yml stage-template.yml'. azure-pipelines.yml is 80 lines, so stage-template refs are +80 (sqlServiceConnection use is :117/:131; cited :197/:211; the file is 158 lines, so :155-238 is impossible). :58, :95-98 and :97-98 are right because those came from other reads. (d) activity.jsonl:307 runs 'cat -n Errors/ResultExtensions.cs Errors/ProblemCatalog.cs'. ResultExtensions.cs is 39 lines, so ProblemCatalog refs are +39 (:50-76 is :11-37 in a 40-line file). (e) activity.jsonl:327 runs 'sed -n 95,188p Policy.cs', which prints no line numbers, so the Policy.cs numbers were counted by hand and drift by 2-11 (Payment!.Method is Policy.cs:167, cited :164-165; texts are :135/:148/:172, cited :128-132/:146/:161). (f) activity.jsonl:306 concatenates appsettings*.json and launchSettings.json without -n (applicationUrl is launchSettings.json:19, cited :22). Separately, claims.json:219 sources README:68 to 'ProblemCatalog.cs:69-74 (the same 12 ids map to 422, 4 to 409, GET-1 to 404)'. No id-to-status map exists. ProblemCatalog.StatusFor maps ViolationKind (:30-35), and the split comes from the kind each rule's violation is built with. That is a wrong description of the source, not just a wrong line. The self-certifying sentence at claims.json:7 was written without any check that compared a cited line with its content. RECURRENCE: new. The table is new in this attempt (inv-003 rec 1). FIX DIRECTION: read each source file on its own with numbered output (one file per numbered read, or grep -n), never a multi-file cat -n and never an unnumbered sed slice. Make every source checkable by machine. Cite path:line plus a short verbatim anchor that appears on that line (for example appservice.bicep:37 'httpsOnly: true'), or a symbol (ProblemCatalog.StatusFor, Policy.Renew), or, for absence claims, a grep pattern and its expected count (for example 'ipSecurityRestrictions' in infrastructure/**/*.bicep = 0). Line numbers then become a convenience that the anchor confirms. Delete the 'correct at daa4876' limit, or replace it with the receipt of a check that verified every anchor. Fix claims.json:219 to name ViolationKind and the rule's violation kind as the source of the 409/422 split.

findings.cause: A cross-cutting method finding, stated separately on purpose and not merged into I1-I5. It is the reason R1-R4 got through a claim trace that existed. SYMPTOM: inv-003 rec 1 was implemented (256 claims), and A3 still finds a false 'so', widened scopes, wider quantifiers and wrong refs. CAUSE: the trace checks that a source exists and is relevant, not that it supports the exact sentence, for four reasons. (1) The 'sentence' field paraphrases instead of quoting, so the words the check needs go missing. claims.json:512 turns design.md:72's 'so' into ';', and claims.json:362 keeps 'All routes' but cites a narrower fact. (2) The sources cited sometimes disprove the sentence: requirements.md:125 for R2, commit-msg:33-45 for R3, PolicyService.cs:56-121 for R3. A source-supports-sentence check would have caught each. (3) inv-003 rec 1 allows 'marked observed/untested' as a way out. claims.json:8 used it to keep a code prediction that contradicts the only observation (I1). (4) The trace vouches for itself (claims.json:7). No independent pass compared anchors with lines, and the reviewer sampled 72 of 256 claims. This is the I14 lineage (A2), but not the same cause. I14 was 'no trace step'; this is 'a trace step that checks presence, not support'. So it gets a new fingerprint, and the per-sentence recurrences in I1 and I2 carry the escalation. A contributing input: the A2 investigator findings put code readings ('rEFERENCE', 'cOLOUR', 'keeps the rest of its casing') into the fix inputs as diagnostic reasoning, and the builder treated them as sources. FIX DIRECTION: the 'sentence' field quotes the doc verbatim, so connectors such as so, because, only, all, every, never and except stay visible. Each source is a verbatim anchor, symbol or grep (I5). For each quantified or causal sentence, the entry names the line that bounds the quantifier or carries the cause. A sentence whose only support is a prediction from code that no test or measurement confirms is removed, not marked. Investigator and verdict prose is never a source.

findings.cause: A4 R2. WHAT THE SENTENCE SAYS: infrastructure/README.md:74-75 reads 'The claim is exactly this: the YAML is valid against the schema; template expansion, `${{ }}` expressions, task inputs, service connections and environments are not checked.' WHAT THE REPO PROVES: the checker does check some of these, but only offline, as text. It asserts that each deploying-stage AzureCLI@2 step has the input keys azureSubscription, scriptType, scriptLocation and inlineScript (check-pipeline.py:83-86). It asserts that every azureSubscription is a `${{ parameters.x }}` expression, by regex (:205-208), and that the SQL connection is passed as a parameter (:209-210). It asserts the environment text 'environment: policies-${{ parameters.environmentName }}' (:112) and the pool-name expression (:213-215). It never expands templates or evaluates expressions. Each file is loaded raw (:28-29), validated against the schema on its own (:37-39), and template references are compared only as strings (:44). It never contacts Azure DevOps (:1). So 'not checked' is false for task inputs, service connections, environments and `${{ }}` expressions, and true only in the sense 'not checked against Azure DevOps'. The next paragraph, infrastructure/README.md:77-79, already says so ('It does not validate those values against Azure DevOps'), so :74-75 and :77-79 contradict each other. CAUSE: :74-75 is the verbatim claim required by checklist row A6 (docs/readme-checklist.md:24, 'Otherwise the claim is exactly: ...'). That wording was written before the A1 and A2 review rounds added the AzureCLI@2, azureSubscription and environment assertions to check-pipeline.py. Its trace entry (claims.json:2105-2108) anchors it to the checklist text, check-pipeline.py:1 and :35, not to the lines that bound 'not checked' (:83-86, :112, :205-208). So the table confirmed that the sentence matched the spec, not that it matched the checker. OBLIGATION: A6 requires an exact, bounded statement of what the schema check does not prove. Adding the missing qualifier keeps that obligation and makes each clause true. FIX DIRECTION: keep the A6 sentence and change only its end. EXACT REPLACEMENT for infrastructure/README.md:74-75: 'The claim is exactly this: the YAML is valid against the schema; template expansion, `${{ }}` expressions, task inputs, service connections and environments are not checked against Azure DevOps.' Keep :77-79 as it is; it now reads as detail, not as a contradiction. CHECKLIST: in docs/readme-checklist.md:24, the quoted claim gets the same ending, and the row gets the note '(wording corrected at F6: "against Azure DevOps" added, because check-pipeline.py asserts the AzureCLI@2 input keys, that every azureSubscription is a template parameter, and the environment name, but never contacts Azure DevOps)'. TRACE: claims.json:2107-2108 and :1621-1622 quote the old text, and the anchor 'P infrastructure/README.md:75:task inputs, service connections and environments are not checked.' (with the full stop) will stop matching. Re-anchor the sentence to check-pipeline.py:1, :28-29, :37-39 and :44 for 'not evaluated/expanded', and to :83-86, :112 and :205-208 for what is asserted. Re-run the anchor check.

findings.cause: A4 R3. The layer is the behaviour being described (domain), as A3 I1-I3 used 'api'. The defect is in prose. WHAT THE SENTENCE SAYS: docs/design.md:173-174 reads 'A term with a claim (COULD-2) or an unpaid renewal term (RENEW-3b) gets no Refund record.' This scopes COULD-2 to a term, as if the claim belongs to one term. WHAT THE REPO PROVES: COULD-2 applies to the whole policy. Policy.cs:257 passes the policy-level HasClaims to RefundCalculator.ForTerm for every term. RefundCalculator.cs:30-32 then returns (COULD-2, 0) for every paid term. RefundCalculator.cs:25-28 returns UNPAID-TERM first for a term with no payment, so that rule wins over a claim. Policy.cs:98 creates a Refund only when Amount > 0. tests/Uinsure.Policies.Domain.Tests/CancelWithClaimTests.cs:98-112 proves it: a claim made in term 1 withholds both terms, including term 2, which hasn't started, and gives refunds []. docs/requirements.md:102 says 'No refund if the policy has a claim'. CAUSE: the sentence is copied from checklist row B6 (docs/readme-checklist.md:41, 'A term with a claim (COULD-2) ...'), so the per-term scope is in the obligation text itself. The trace entry (claims.json:1049-1052) cites RefundCalculator.cs:30 'hasClaims' and CancelWithClaimTests (single-term). Both name the subject, but :30 actually bounds it policy-wide, and nobody compared the source with the quantifier. RECURRENCE: this is the A3 I4 cause again, in the same file. A table source names the subject but does not bound the quantifier, and the A3 fix narrowed only the three cited sentences, not the pattern. So I reuse I4's fingerprint. FIX DIRECTION: state the scope COULD-2 actually has, and keep the rest of the paragraph. EXACT REPLACEMENT for docs/design.md:173-175: 'A cancellation creates a Refund only for an amount above £0. If the policy has a claim (COULD-2), none of its paid terms gets a Refund record; an unpaid renewal term (RENEW-3b) gets none either. Their calculations are still in the response, with `ruleApplied` `COULD-2` or `UNPAID-TERM` and `refundAmount` 0.00.' CHECKLIST: docs/readme-checklist.md:41 (B6) has the same scope error, and the reviewer did not raise it. The orchestrator asked only about A4 and A6, so I am raising it here, not merging it silently. Give B6 the same wording plus '(wording corrected at F6: COULD-2 withholds every paid term of a policy with a claim, because Policy.cs passes the policy's HasClaims for each term)'. TRACE: re-source claims.json:1049-1052 to Policy.cs:257, RefundCalculator.cs:25 and :30-32, Policy.cs:98 and Domain CancelWithClaimTests.cs:102. Update the B6 row claim near claims.json:1835-1838. Re-run the anchor check.

findings.cause: A4 R4. WHAT THE SENTENCE SAYS: README.md:66 reads '**No £0 Refund record is created.** The cancellation response still lists every term with `refundAmount` 0.00.' With no comma and no qualifier, it says every term has 0.00. WHAT THE REPO PROVES: every term is listed. Policy.cs:257 calculates every term, Policy.cs:92 and :107 put all the calculations into the decision, and CancellationContracts.cs:23 returns the Terms list. Terms with an amount keep their amount (CancelRenewedPolicyTests.cs:68-69: 17.36 and 512.66). A term shows 0.00 only when its calculation is 0, and that is not limited to COULD-2 and UNPAID-TERM. A term that is already over is CANCEL-1c 0.00 with no refund (CancelRenewedPolicyTests.cs:88-89, :116 and :157). CAUSE: the sentence condenses docs/requirements.md:108 ('still lists every term, with `refundAmount` 0.00 and `ruleApplied` `COULD-2` or `UNPAID-TERM`') and drops both the comma and the ruleApplied qualifier that scope 'every term' to the no-Refund terms. Its trace entry (claims.json:274-278) cites requirements.md:108 with the comma, plus Policy.cs:257, and so supports 'every term is listed', not 'every term is 0.00'. A3 raised this as a non-blocking note, and it went unchanged. This is the same quantifier-scope class as I3 but a different file, so it gets a new fingerprint. FIX DIRECTION: say that every term is listed, and that the zero ones are included. Don't restore requirements.md:108's 'COULD-2 or UNPAID-TERM' list in the README. Read as exhaustive, it would leave out the CANCEL-1c 0.00 of a finished term, which would create a new overreach. EXACT REPLACEMENT for README.md:66: '- **No £0 Refund record is created.** The cancellation response still lists every term, including those with `refundAmount` 0.00.' This is truer than the reviewer's 'each such term', whose antecedent ('£0' in the bold clause) is weak. TRACE: update claims.json:274-278 to quote the new sentence. Source it to Policy.cs:257, Policy.cs:107, CancellationContracts.cs:23, Api CancelWithClaimTests.cs:47 and CancelRenewedPolicyTests.cs:116. Re-run the anchor check. NOTE, not in F6's scope: docs/requirements.md:108 is accurate only as 'every such term'. David may want that row read in the same way.

findings.raw:
# D1: stylesheet dispatch budget raised to 12

At wave 2, patterns-b failed two `field` tests. A retry would have been dispatch 7 of 9, and waves 3 and 4
still needed 3, so the stage would have ended at 10, over the efficiency.spec stylesheet budget.

David's answer: "Raise cap to 12". The per-batch cap stays at 3 attempts. The efficiency.spec amendment
follows as a harness PR.

# D2: alignment defects in the kit, carried into the screens stage

David at G3: "I noticed some alignment issues especially with errors and error icons", "I think there are
lots in place please review the review.html visually", and "a huge chunk of the review file is empty". On
the budget: "Fix it in the screens stage". No kit batch is regenerated; these go to G4.

The main session reviewed per-component screenshots at 1440 and measured overflow at 1440 and 390, at
David's request. Owning batch in brackets.

## Errors and error icons

1. Invalid inputs grow wider than their valid state: text-input, date-input, text-area, select and
   money-input each add an icon slot outside the box, so the field jumps width (primitives-b).
2. The in-field error icon is placed at a fixed offset, not at the right edge: on money-input it sits on
   top of the right-aligned digits; on select it is jammed against the chevron (primitives-b).
3. Two icons per error: the message carries one and the input carries another (primitives-b, field).
4. Two error message styles: the primitives' message is small with a smaller icon and wraps early
   ("2026-10-" / "19."), while inline-error is larger and bold (primitives-b, patterns-b).
5. inline-error "several on one field" shows the icon and a bullet together on the first item, so the
   items don't align (patterns-b).
6. field "invalid" pushes the label, hint and input right of the plain fields by the width of its error
   bar, and the invalid input is wider than the plain one (patterns-b).
7. form-section and repeatable-group with errors: the inputs run past the right edge of the grey card
   (measured 674 against 672) (patterns-b).
8. radio-group invalid: the icon in the legend and the error bar indent the options away from the valid
   state (primitives-b).

## Other alignment and layout

9. The dashed left rule (problem-banner unreachable, verdict-card lost) renders as heavy blocks
   (patterns-b, project-a).
10. agent-lanes: the lanes run past the pane and are clipped; "refactor" breaks as "refact / or" in the
    TDD column (project-a).
11. status-tag "both themes" nests a light pane inside the dark pane (primitives-a).
12. Horizontal overflow: the page is 1809 wide at 1440 (app-shell frames to 2180, agent-lanes to 1838,
    markdown-text code to 1485), and 1099 wide at 390 (also refund-worked-sum, request-log, data-table,
    quote-cancel-compare, dag-graph, dag-table, the inputs and text-area) (layout, project, patterns).

## At sign-off

David, on the per-state review (#36): "over 2 dp invalid by rule = error icon over the numeric values -
other than those it looks good". That is item 2 (money-input), confirmed. He signed G3 off with D2 carried
to G4. Tabular figures in the T5 faces were not checked at G3, so they stay open for the screens stage.

## The review page (a harness defect, not a kit one)

13. audit-kit takes one full-page screenshot per width: 1809 × 87,052 and 1099 × 218,095 pixels.
    Chromium can't paint a capture that tall, so most of each image is blank. The review needs one shot
    per component section instead.

skills.name: architecture

skills.name: creative-direction
skills.description: The method the creative-director runs to turn research into three divergent, cited design territories for Docket's two halves: concept first, layout derived, excludes that stop re-convergence, one signature move per half, a derived palette that passes contrast.
